clue.text: Loud type of musician hasn't finished cold drink

indicators.note: something that has not finished stops short, so the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
a rapper is one kind of musician

explanation.surface: A noisy sort of performer leaves a chilled drink half-drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The accent on frappé is ignored in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A frappé is a drink served iced or shaken with crushed ice, such as iced coffee.

clue.text: I ask chef to change this bit of seafood

indicators.note: to change these letters is to rearrange them into a new word

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner asks the chef to swap a seafood dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishcake is a patty of flaked fish and potato, a small portion of seafood.

clue.text: Weapon comrade carries back

indicators.note: a word that carries something holds it inside, so the letters lie within
back tells us to read the run of letters from right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A fellow soldier lugs a weapon behind.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm is a weapon, as in firearms or a call to arms.

clue.text: Peg worked to dissipate a potential disaster

indicators.note: to dissipate is to scatter, so the letters are dispersed and regathered in another order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Peg laboured to head off a looming catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A powder keg is a barrel of gunpowder, figuratively a tense situation that could explode.

clue.text: City witches go for

blocks.note: a coven is a gathering of witches
to go for something is to have a try at it

explanation.surface: A city that witches set out to reach.
explanation.walkthrough: Coventry is a city in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Coventry is an English city in the West Midlands, so it is an example of the category named.

clue.text: Seasoning duck with orange puree

indicators.note: a puree is food mashed to a pulp, so these letters are mashed into a new order

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A herb rub for duck à l'orange.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a herb used to flavour food, especially Italian and Greek dishes.

clue.text: Leaders in English lad's newspaper upset scorer

indicators.note: leaders are the front-runners, so just the opening letter of each word
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

blocks.note: the first letters of these two words
a rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: A boy's paper is cross with the goal scorer in its headlines.
explanation.walkthrough: Scorer suggests sport; here it is one who writes musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edward Elgar was an English composer, someone who writes scores of music.

clue.text: Troops initially told Ben-Hur about bombshell

indicators.note: initially points to the very first letter only
about suggests the letters are moved around into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the first letter
the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers break shocking news to the hero of the epic film.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a thunderbolt and a bombshell are sudden shocking surprises, used figuratively.

clue.text: The old dean got up and made a lot of noise

indicators.note: got up in a down clue means rose, so the word reads upwards

blocks.note: ye is the archaic spelling of the
a dean or dene is a small wooded valley, as is a dell

explanation.surface: The elderly college dean rose and caused a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: Dean looks like a college official, but it is a dialect word for a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: To yell is to shout loudly, so someone who yelled made a great noise.

clue.text: Once, return service

blocks.note: first meaning, archaic as 'once' signals: to go back to a place
second meaning: to fix or maintain a machine

explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks an old sense: to repair was to return; it survives in 'repair to the drawing room'.
explanation.definitionFit: To service a car is to overhaul it, and an obsolete sense of the verb is going back somewhere.

clue.text: Few heard to put on Bernstein classic

indicators.note: heard tells us to take the sound of the phrase it follows rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a few means some
to put on clothes is to wear them, and wear is pronounced like where

explanation.surface: Not many people heard a Bernstein favourite being staged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' suggests staging the music, but it means wearing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere is the famous song by Leonard Bernstein from the musical West Side Story.

clue.text: Good game against the Spanish but it was disappointing fare

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
RU is rugby union
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A sports report: a fine match against Spain, but a let-down for the spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against' just places the Spanish article next to the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruel is thin porridge, proverbially meagre and unappetising food.

clue.text: Fancy leaders of radio appear after jingle

indicators.note: the leaders of words are the letters at their front, so only the opening letter of each counts
after places the letters from the radio phrase behind the jingle's word

blocks.note: a chime is a ringing, jingling sound
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Fancy radio stations putting the jingle first.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a wild illusion or fantasy, which is what a fancy can mean as a noun.

clue.text: Doctor retires with this best friend

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered in order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor going into retirement takes their faithful dog along.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor looks like a person, but it is the verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog is called man's best friend, and this red-coated gundog breed is a dog.

clue.text: Shorten a spanner

blocks.note: first meaning: to cut down a text
second meaning, split into two words: a structure that spans a river or road

explanation.walkthrough: A spanner looks like a tool, but here it is something that spans; read the answer as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a book is to condense it; a bridge is literally a thing that spans a gap.

clue.text: Clobber thief, say, with obstructions left out

indicators.note: left out means the letter for left is taken away from the word

blocks.note: a whimsical word for one who nicks, that is steals; 'say' flags the invention
blockers are things that obstruct
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Hit a thief with the barricades removed.
explanation.walkthrough: Clobber looks like a verb meaning hit, but it is British slang for clothes; 'nick' is British slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Knickerbockers are loose breeches gathered at the knee, a garment, and clobber is slang for clothing.

clue.text: Peckish delivery person?

blocks.note: surface reading: a hungry courier
setter's reading: given to pecks, that is kisses, delivered as a novelty greeting

explanation.walkthrough: Peckish means slightly hungry in British English, but a peck is also a light kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a novelty greeting where a hired person arrives to deliver a kiss, a peck, to the recipient.

clue.text: Fancy planes might be flown thus?

blocks.note: first meaning: an exclamation of surprise, like 'fancy that!'
second meaning: George is the pilots' nickname for the autopilot

explanation.walkthrough: Aircrew have long called the automatic pilot 'George', so a plane on autopilot is flown by him.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an old-fashioned oath of surprise, and literally says who is at the controls.

clue.text: Long-haired Harry's blue gag

blocks.note: shaggy means having long, rough hair
to harry is to dog, someone's pursuit; the apostrophe S adds the S
blue is the colour of the Conservatives, the Tories

explanation.surface: A shaggy-haired man called Harry tells a smutty joke.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry looks like a name and blue like 'risqué'; Tory is a UK Conservative, whose party colour is blue.
explanation.definitionFit: A long rambling joke with a deliberately feeble punchline is a classic kind of gag.

clue.text: Distance, say, a cart reversed

indicators.note: reversed tells us to write the whole sequence backwards

blocks.note: eg, for example, means say
taken as written
a dray is a low flat cart for heavy loads

explanation.surface: How far, for instance, a cart backed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardage is a distance measured in yards, as in American football.

clue.text: Business raised some support with unknown people

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means lifted up, so the word reads bottom to top

blocks.note: Co is short for company
a cup is part of a bra, which gives support
y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A firm raises backing alongside some mystery individuals.
explanation.walkthrough: People is a verb here, not a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To people a place is to fill it with inhabitants, just as to occupy it is to live there.

clue.text: Old car key — something that wasn't wanted

blocks.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard
an ort is a scrap of food left over

explanation.surface: A car key from an old banger: something nobody wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ford Escort was a popular British family car.
explanation.definitionFit: The Escort was a Ford model sold from the 1960s to the 2000s, now a vintage vehicle.

clue.text: Undercover agent?

blocks.note: surface reading: a spy working secretly in enemy territory
setter's reading: someone literally under the bedclothes, dozing

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses fit: a dormant spy planted to wait for orders, and one tucked in under the covers.
explanation.definitionFit: In espionage the term means a planted spy lying dormant, and it also means anyone asleep in bed.

clue.text: Navy officer's nicked bag

indicators.note: nicked means cut slightly, so a bit is trimmed off the end

blocks.note: a purser is the officer in charge of a ship's accounts

explanation.surface: A naval officer's handbag has been stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicked reads as British slang for stolen, but here it means trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: A purse is a small pouch for money, a kind of handbag.

clue.text: Retiring officer engaged in boring work? What a laugh!

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the officer is written backwards
to be engaged in something is to be inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a chore is a tedious task
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: An officer about to retire is stuck with dull work: some joke!
explanation.definitionFit: A chortle is a gleeful chuckle, a kind of laugh; the word was coined by Lewis Carroll.

clue.text: Fur making cockney thus?

indicators.note: a cockney Londoner traditionally drops the H at the start of words

blocks.note: 'thus' is the state fur leaves its wearer in: warmer

explanation.surface: Fur coats leave a London cockney feeling the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: Wearing fur makes you warmer, and a cockney, a working-class Londoner, would pronounce that comparative without its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Otter is the dense brown pelt of the river animal, prized as a fur.

clue.text: Like a lot of Silver, say, and Gold medical equipment

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: as means like
Long John Silver of Treasure Island is an example of a pirate
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Something that looks like silver and gold, but is a hospital device.
explanation.walkthrough: Silver and Gold look like metals; only Gold is, and Silver is the pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirator is a suction device used in medicine to draw fluid from the body.

clue.text: Duck left concealed leaves

indicators.note: concealed means hidden away, so that letter vanishes from the word

blocks.note: a teal is a small duck
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A duck hid among the foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaves looks like a verb or foliage; it is the dried leaves brewed as a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is made from the dried leaves of the tea plant, often simply called leaves.

clue.text: Author's short book about most of Swiss city

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the book's name loses its last letter
about can mean turned round, so the shortened book is written backwards
most of a word is all but its final letter

blocks.note: Ruth is a book of the Old Testament
Geneva is a city in Switzerland

explanation.surface: A writer's slim volume about a Swiss city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' is the Bible's Ruth; shortened and turned round, it starts the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was a 19th-century Russian novelist, the writer of Fathers and Sons.

clue.text: Spike Sprite with a stronger drink

blocks.note: a sprite is an elf or imp
beer is stronger than the soft drink Sprite

explanation.surface: Lace a lemonade with something more alcoholic.
explanation.walkthrough: Sprite reads as the soft drink, and spike as adding alcohol; in fact Sprite is a mischievous spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale is to pierce something with a sharp point, as a spike does.
